A Monopoly on Spies
Aryon suggested that I introduce myself to Galas Drenim and gain an understanding of politics on Vvardenfell.

Galas Drenim explained some details about politics on the Grand Council but pointed out that these surface level politics are augmented with tactics involving spies and assassination. She suggested that I speak to Endar Drenim about the mages guild monopoly.

I've agreed to help remove one of the problematic Mages Guild spies for Endar Drenim. He gave me a note which I am to deliver to Chanil-Lee at the Six Fishes in Ebonheart. I will need to confirm she is dead after the custom enchantment summons a daedra to kill her.
I have delivered the enchanted note to Chanil-Lee.
Chanil-Lee is dead. Endar Drenim will be pleased to hear this.
Endar Drenim thanked me for dispatching one of the mages guild spies. He rewarded me with several heavy coin purses.
Endar Drenim thanked me for dispatching one of the mages guild spies. He rewarded me with valuable enchanted scrolls.
How Dratha's Garden Grows
Liela of Tel Mora asked me to bring her 5 gold kanet flowers to increase the varieties of plants in Mistress Dratha's gardens.
I brought Liela the 5 gold kanet that she needed. She told me to come back when I am ready to do more work.
The next thing Liela wants me to get for her are 3 trama root cuttings.
I brought Liela the 3 trama root that she needed. She told me to come back when I am ready to do more work.
Liela sent me to try to find Timsa-Come-By flowers at the High Fane in Vivec. She said that pilgrims sometimes leave them there as offerings.
Liela thanked me for bringing her the 4 Timsa-Come-By flowers and rewarded me with a Totem of Zeht.
Apply Pressure to the Wound
Berel Sala was offended that I asked for compensation to speak with Mistress Dratha about bringing healers to Tel Mora, but promised to pay me for the work.
Charity of Bone and Steel

Radras in Tel Mora asked me to talk to Godros in the Tel Branora Guardpost about her limited stock of steel armor. It sounds like she has been shipping armor with no compensation from Mistress Therana's underlings.
Godros mentioned "Trerayna Dalen" and suggested that I speak with Mollimo of Cloudrest who patrols outside of the Tel Branora tower.

Mollimo of Cloudrest thinks Trerayna Dalen was placing the orders for armor to Radras herself but under the guise of Godros. He said he will secure the docks to ensure no more shipments are intercepted. I should discuss compensation for Radras with Godros.

Godros gave me payment for the two crates of steel he received but said he couldn't compensate Radras for the armor Trerayna Dalen intercepted. I should report back to Radras on the investigation of her limited stock.
I gave Radras the payment from Godros for the two crates of steel armor. She gave me some back as payment and said she'd give me better prices from now on.
I lied and told Radras that Godros refused to give me any payment for the steel shipment. She said she would have to increase prices to compensate for the lost profit.
An Illusion of Time
Tel Mora appears to be under attack.
I slew one of the monsters attacking Tel Mora, but it reanimated in front of my eyes. Dratha will be no help, I should seek Aryon's advice.
Aryon asked me to talk to Endar Drenim about the vampires attacking Tel Mora. He thinks that Endar can use his illusion magic to help.

Endar Drenim gave me a copy of his notes for a powerful spell he thinks could be used to save Tel Mora from the vampire attack. He asked me to take it to the Master of Illusion: Erer Darothil at Dirty Muriel's Cornerclub in Sadrith Mora. Endar has not been able to cast the spell successfully and he hopes that Erer will be able to offer advice.

I took Endar's Theory to Erer Darothil as requested. Erer advised that the target needs to be given a specific mark in order to avoid wasting the caster's energy. I should bring this information back to Endar Drenim.
Endar immediately worked out how to alter the spell, but he needs a portion of vampire dust and corprus weepings to properly focus it.

I brought Endar the vampire dust and corprus weepings required to correct the influx spell. He used them to enchant a scroll which he gave me with instructions to use it on the stone altar beneath Dratha's tower. He suggested that she might keep another way to access the underground part of her tower in her private chambers.
Something happened after I used the scroll on the stone table underneath Tel Mora. I should check to see if the vampires are still attacking Tel Mora.
Tel Mora is no longer under attack. I should talk to Aryon.

Aryon thanked me for working with Endar Drenim to deal with the vampires attacking Tel Mora. As a reward, he gave me a dwemer sword named Dissonance. He mentioned that we should discuss how to deal with Dratha now that it's clear she is not fit to rule Tel Mora.
I heard a rumor in Tel Mora that the temple has been pressuring Mistress Dratha to allow them to put some healers in Tel Mora. I should speak with a member of the Tribunal Temple to learn more.
I have been directed to Berel Sala at the Justice Offices in Vivec to learn more about the Temple pressuring Mistress Dratha.
I have agreed to talk to Mistress Dratha about allowing some healers in Tel Mora.
Mistress Dratha had no interest in allowing healers in Tel Mora. Perhaps I could speak to someone else in the town about how to approach this situation.
After Dratha's firm dismissal of the healers in Tel Mora topic, I spoke with someone in Tel Mora who recommended that I speak with her Mouth, Raven Omayn at the Council House in Sadrith Mora.

Raven Omayn was not surprised that Dratha was unwilling to discuss the subject of healers in Tel Mora, but said that may change once the trouble under Tel Mora has been dealt with. I agreed to look into it, and she gave me an index stone which I can use within the town of Tel Mora to be teleported underneath the city. I can use it again at any time to return.
It would seem that the "trouble under Tel Mora" is a haunting of some sort of vampiric monsters. I should kill all of them that I can find and return to Raven.

I believe that I have disposed of all the vampires. It appears that Mistress Dratha has been conducting some very dangerous experiments underneath her tower... I should return to Raven with the index and report my success.
Raven told me that Mistress Dratha will be pleased that I took care of the trouble under Tel Mora and that now would be a good time to approach her about allowing healers in Tel Mora.

Mistress Dratha finally agreed to allow the Temple to send healers to the town of Tel Mora on 3 conditions: First, they must be women. Second, the Temple must pay property and boarding rent on the last Loredas of every month. Third, she never wants to see an Ordinator set foot in Tel Mora again. I worry that Berel Sala will not be pleased about her last condition.
Berel Sala agreed to Mistress Dratha's conditions. Mistress Dratha may be interested to know of it.
Mistress Dratha was very pleased with Berel Sala's response and said the new mushroom pod for the Temple healer's should be completed in a week.
The new pod for the healers in Tel Mora should be completed by now.
Dratha's Collections
I stole an item from Mistress Dratha's collections. She will not be pleased.
I tried to approach Mistress Dratha after stealing from her collections and she blasted me into another realm...
Master Endar

With Dratha out of the picture, Aryon said that everything is already in motion to make Endar Drenim the new Master of Tel Mora. He suggested that I go speak with Endar as he will be relocating soon and Aryon expects he will want to thank me in person.
Endar thanked me for telling him about Dratha's geas. He gifted me with an enchanted hood. He should be moving to Tel Mora soon.
I decided not to tell Endar about Dratha's geas. He gifted me with an enchanted hood. He should be moving to Tel Mora soon.
Endar Drenim should have moved to Tel Mora by now.
Vote of No Confidence
I've refused to help Aryon deal with Dratha.

Aryon says that Dratha is too unreliable to leave in control of Tel Mora. I have agreed to speak with Sonummu Zabamat, the Wise Woman of the Zainab Ashlander tribe in the Grazelands, about how to deal with Dratha's geas. The geas is a curse which will be unleashed on whoever kills her. Aryon thinks that Sonummu will have some way to counter it since the geas is Mabrigash magic.

I have met with Sonummu Zabamat. After I asked her about how to deal with Dratha, she briefly explained geasa to me. Aryon's description of Dratha's geas jogged something in Sonummu's memory and she asked me to leave while she meditates. I may come back in a day.
Sonummu placed a counter-geas on me which should offer protection from Dratha's curse. I should discuss with Aryon before doing anything.
I've let Aryon know that I have the counter-geas. It's time to confront Dratha.
After I killed Dratha, her body disappeared in a blast of magic. Possibly due to the geas. I'm not sure that I would feel anything, but I don't think it affected me. I should speak to Aryon.
Aryon thanked me for dispatching Dratha. He didn't seem concerned that her body disappeared. Now he wants to talk about Endar Drenim.
After talking to Sonummu Zabamat, I have refused to help Aryon deal with Dratha. He will have to find some other way to help Tel Mora.
Tel Mora Healer Supplies

I have agreed to help Edrelle Mene, one of the new Temple healers in Tel Mora, with stocking their supplies: 5 potions of cure common disease, 3 potions of cure blight disease, 8 corkbulb root cuttings, and 8 marshmerrow clippings.
I delivered the items from Edrelle Mene's list to her and she paid me back the value of the items plus extra.
Dratha's Memory Stones
I found a memory stone underneath Tel Mora. It appears to be part of a set. Perhaps the others are around here somewhere.
I found a set of memory stones from Dratha underneath her tower. Perhaps these will be of use to someone.
I told Mehra Othan about Dratha's memory stones. She believes they might be the reason for Borwen's condition.
Borwen's Headache

Mehra Othan tried to talk to me about the various ailments people from Tel Mora had come to the new Temple healers with already. When she mentioned Borwen, I let her know I was not interested in discussing the subject further.

I have agreed to bring Mehra Othan's letter to Yakin Bael, the Master of Restoration who can be found at the Vos Chapel just west from Tel Mora. Mehra Othan mentioned that I can take the boat from Tel Mora.
Yakin Bael gave me a letter to take back to Mehra Othan.
I brought Yakin Bael's letter back to Mehra Othan.

After discussing Borwen's various ailments with Mehra Othan, we settled on the need to venture underneath Dratha's tower to find a clue to what might be affecting Borwen's mind. Mehra Othan suggested that I look out for some type of artifact related to the mind or memories.
Mehra Othan asked me to discuss Dratha's memory stones with Yakin Bael in the Vos Chapel.
Yakin Bael's only recommendation was for Mehra Othan to continue giving salves to Borwen.
Mehra Othan thanked me for my help investigating the various ailments which were afflicting Borwen of Tel Mora and offered to provide me healing for free from now on.
After I cured Lette, she returned to her work in the Tel Mora gardens.
Master Endar agreed to vote for me as Hortator of House Telvanni.

After hearing my story, Master Aryon agreed to make me the Telvanni Hortator. He said the other councilors might need some persuading. Master Neloth is ill-tempered, Mistress Therana is losing her mind, and Master Endar will be a formality. Master Aryon told me that Archmagister Gothren would delay my request indefinitely. He advised me to kill Archmagister Gothren.
I already have my orders, %PCName.
Thank you.

That should be it. I wish I could do this myself, but with what I believe Master Aryon has planned, I need to keep my distance from Tel Mora for a little while longer. You'll see why soon enough. So take this scroll. I know thereis a stone altar underneath Tel Mora. You might have seen it. If you don't have a way to get back down there, search Dratha's chambers. You will need to cast the spell from that altar. The ruins beneath her tower are a powerful magical location and will amplify its effects.
Give me a moment.

It's so obvious! Of course the Law of Intensification would work in reverse in this case. I can alter the spell to look for a specific set of targets, but I'll need something to focus it... vampire dust. And you mentioned these vampires were also corprus victims? I'll need some corprus weepings as well.
You must bring my notes to Erer Darothil.

If it works as intended, the smallest parts of an individual's body will enter into stasis. Completely cut off from reality. Maybe even including time itself. Well, at least in theory. Here are some of my notes. I've edited them to seem less... alarming to those with certain sensibilities. Can you take it to Erer Darothil? He's currently staying at Dirty Muriel's Cornerclub here in Sadrith Mora. He's a Master of Illusion and has been tutoring me when I have time for my own research.

Master Aryon wants me to get involved with this situation? Yes. I see. Very well. As it turns out, this sounds like a prime opportunity to conduct an experiment of my own! And save the inhabitants of the city, of course. If it works, anyway... I've come up with a new spell effect founded on illusory principles but I've never been able to get it to work, you see. In theory, it should overwhelm the target's faculties with sensory input having an effect similar to paralysis.

Well done, %PCName. I know you're accustomed to getting the credit for grand deeds such as this, but I ask you to allow me to direct most of the praise to Endar Drenim. I need the people of Tel Mora to see him as their savior. I want to give you something as a token of my gratitude for handling this with such finesse.

Well done, %PCName. I know you're accustomed to getting the credit for grand deeds such as this, but I ask you to allow me to direct most of the praise to Endar Drenim. As I said before, we must deal with Dratha. And he's the key to it. I need the people of Tel Mora to see him as their savior. But before we rush into that subject, I want to give you something as a token of my gratitude for handling this with such finesse.
You must work with Endar Drenim to put an end to this madness.

I'm trying to keep it contained to Tel Mora. I'm glad you're here. We will deal with Dratha's inaction soon, but first, we must secure the safety of everyone in Tel Mora. I must ask you to speak with Endar Drenim again. He is a student of Illusion and I think he can help. I know it doesn't intimidating enough for this situation, but I think he's just what Tel Mora needs right now. If brute force won't work, then perhaps subtlety will.

I'm trying to keep it contained to Tel Mora. I'm glad you're here. We must secure the safety of everyone in Tel Mora. I must ask you to speak with Endar Drenim again. He is a student of Illusion and I think he can help. I know it doesn't intimidating enough for this situation, but I think he's just what Tel Mora needs right now. If brute force won't work, then perhaps subtlety will.
Very well. Like this...
As I suspected. Good luck in your meeting with Mistress Dratha.
You don't have the index with you. Why don't you fetch it if you want to return it?

A conservative choice, %PCName. But I respect your decision. Mistress Dratha is not to be trifled with. Here, take these potions I made with some vampire dust. And if you like, I can teach you a spell to cure blight disease and other ailments. It's a very complex spell, I doubt you'll even be able to cast it properly.
We never had this conversation.

It is the Telvanni way. If you have the power to take something, take it. But be ready to deal with the consequences. I have warned you already about what Mistress Dratha might do if she were to catch you after having her collections raided.

You managed to dispose of all the experiments? Mistress Dratha will be very pleased and I can say with confidence that she'll be willing to talk with you about the Temple healers now. Now you have a choice to make, %PCName: you can give me back the index stone and I can give you a reward appropriate for your aid or I can pretend you never came back to return the stone and you are free to do what you will with that access...
Be wary while under the tower, %PCName. Mistress Dratha has been delving into dangerous experiments of late. But which Telvanni Lord hasn't?

Very well, %PCName. Take this index and grasp it in your hand while in Tel Mora and you'll be transported underneath the town. You can use it to return above ground any time while you're down there if things get too hazardous. Oh, and a word of warning: don't touch anything from Mistress Dratha's collections. She has powerful traps placed upon them which I don't suspect you could survive. And even if you do, you can forget about her considering to allow healers in Tel Mora from the Temple if you steal any.
Understandable. I don't expect the problem to go away anytime soon. Come back if you change your mind.

Under normal circumstances, only Mistress Dratha, Sadela Areth, and myself are permitted into the roots of Tel Mora. But one of Mistress Dratha's recent experiments has gone awry and she hasn't been able to go down there to look at her collections in some time. If you're interested, I can get you in to deal with the situation.

Master Endar is our new Telvanni mage-lord patron. Everyone feels safer and more optimistic about the city's future under his guidance. Thaeril is the publican at the Covenant. And there's Berwen the trader, Radras the smith, Elegnan the clothier, and Jolda the apothecary.

It's a pleasure to speak to the %PCRace who helped precipitate the decline of the Mages Guild here in Morrowind. You may have already realized this, but beyond the other Great Houses, the Imperial Mages Guild is one of our primary competitors. Not only economically, but magically. They have been increasingly sticking their bespelled fingers into affairs which do not concern them. Mages guild spies have infiltrated many locations and are proving a hindrance to our own espionage efforts.

According to one interpretation of the Armistice, only the Mages Guild can officially offer spells and training to non-members. Speak with the House Redoran Councilors in Ald'ruhn. If you can convince at least three Councilors, we will have enough support in the Grand Council. I would start with Athyn Sarethi as he seems to be the most open-minded.
You were a great help with Mistress Dratha's garden. Tending such a beautiful plot of... roots is a pleasure.

These flowers will look terrific in the garden. Your help has been invaluable and Lette and I want to give you something meaningful as a token of our appreciation. Please accept this small amulet with Zeht's blessing.
That's not enough, %PCName.
Come back when you have to be compensated.
Did you find the four Timsa-Come-By flowers that I need?

Now, I'm not going to ask you to hike all the way to Southeastern Morrowind to pick some flowers. I heard that Indoril pilgrims sometimes leave the flowers as offerings at the High Fane in Vivec. Maybe you can find some there; four flowers will be enough. I should be able to get enough seeds from that many.

Mistress Dratha wants her garden to be the only one on Vvardenfell which grows Timsa-Come-By flowers. These flowers aren't native to the island, you see. Apparently this request is something personal for her -- name of a childhood friend or something is the impression I got. She's not often sentimental, so I'd like to satisfy this request.

Thank you, %PCName. These will do nicely. Mistress Dratha gave Lette and me a bonus for the last harvest and we want you to have a portion as a token of our appreciation. The next thing Mistress Dratha wanted is a little more special. Come back when you are ready for more work.
Did you find the three trama thorns that I need?

Now, the next thing Mistress Dratha specifically requested were some trama shrubs. They are naturally an invasive species so I will simply take a few of the root thorns and graft them to a hackle-lo plant to contain their growth. I believe the thorns themselves (even when grafted) can grow into a full root to produce more of the thorns which can be used as cuttings in alchemical brews. Three thorns should be enough.

Superb work, %PCName. This will be just enough to grow a few gold kanet flowers here. Here are some potions from Jolda as payment -- hopefully they'll help you get around a bit more easily around here. Come back when you're ready to help some more.
Did you find the five gold kanet flowers that I need?

Then you've got the job, %PCName. The first thing Dratha wants is gold kanet. Right now, House Hlaalu has the kagouti's share of gold kanet blooms in the alchemical market. Gold kanet has a tough time growing naturally in the soil of Azura's Coast, but we came up with a special blend of minerals which should make the soil more habitable for a modest growth here. If you bring me five gold kanet flowers, that should be enough. I'd recommend searching in the Ascadian Isles region.
This isn't an urgent task as far as I am concerned. Feel free to come back later if you change your mind.

Before Lette caught the swamp fever, Mistress Dratha tasked us with introducing more variety to her garden to increase profits from ingredient exports. Since Lette and I are so busy with the garden now, I won't have time to go and gather them for a while. Would you be interested in taking the job? We can compensate you for your work performed.
That's us.
Yes we are.
Yes, they are here.
We've received word that the new healers have been sent for and should arrive right at the time the pod is complete.

Berel Sala, the high and mighty Captain of the Watch said that? Oh, what I'd give to have seen the look on his face. And sensible of him to agree to all of my conditions. I expected that outcome and already began cultivating the sprout for the new pod. Another week or so and it'll be large enough to inhabit.
Thank you for your help with establishing healers in Tel Mora. The people there will not have to suffer as Lette did.

By Boethiah's puckered ass! That diddling old woman likes to poke the kagouti. Fine. Her conditions will be met. The healers will be women and will be furnished with appropriate funds for rent. As to the last... well, I truly have no need to visit Tel Mora with Vos so nearby. But were I to find a reason... there's nothing Dratha could do to stop the Ordinators. In any case, you've done good work, %PCClass. Here, take your reward. You've earned it.
Conditions? That tiresome old hag. Well, let's hear them then. Come on, I haven't got all day.
Return after you have spoken with Berel Sala.
I would be disappointed if he didn't. You will report back on his exact facial expression when you recite my litany.
Run along, %PCClass.

A compelling argument, %PCName. Better the scamp you know... [Dratha pauses in thought.] Carry a message back to the dear Berel Sala and let him know that Tel Mora will allow healers from the Temple on three conditions. First, they must be women. Second, the Temple must pay property and boarding rent on the last Loredas of every month. Third, I never want to see an Ordinator set foot in Tel Mora again.
Of course I could, but why would I when I am comfortable now; without any meddling priestesses here?
You are dense, aren't you? They're not interested in helping, we don't need their help.
You are dense, even for a %PCRace, aren't you? They're not interested in helping, we don't need their help.
Dangerously presumptuous of you, %PCRace. I can handle the Temple myself.

Yes, Jolda is not reliable at treating ailments herself and Lette's prolonged illness was wasteful -- and unfortunate. But the Temple is a charity of meddling old windbags. I cannot trust their priests not to stick their noses where they don't belong.
We already have an apothecary, why should I need healers as well?

Raven told me of your success in dealing with the small issue under my tower. Were you bitten? Scratched? Let me see your eyes... now you wanted to talk to me about allowing Temple spies into my town?
Now that you've dealt with the trouble under Tel Mora, Mistress Dratha should be more approachable on this subject.
Perhaps once you've dealt with the trouble under Tel Mora, Mistress Dratha will be more amenable to discuss the topic again.

Oh, you spoke to Dratha about this touchy subject and she didn't blast you into Oblivion on the spot? Well, she has been rather distracted by the trouble under Tel Mora recently. Perhaps if you help with that, she will be more amenable to discuss the topic again.
[Whispers] I can't talk about that right now. Dratha might hear.

I'm not surprised that Mistress Dratha has no interest in allowing the Temple to establish a shrine here. She and the Temple have a disagreeable history from what I hear. Maybe you should speak to her Mouth, Raven Omayn, in Sadrith Mora and see if she has any ideas.
Let's not speak of this.
Now you're just being stupid, even for a man. Get. Out.
As much as I appreciate your tenacity, I already gave the belligerent Ordinators who swept through here my answer: we do not need any healers in Tel Mora.

Did you hear something, Sadela? Oh it's a man slithering in here to beg for me to let some Temple spies into our town. I believe I let those belligerent Ordinators know where I stood on the matter in no uncertain terms. No.
Report back when you have an update on the situation.
I believe that your humility is not the correct tool for this task, %PCRank. But I am heartened by your desire to serve Almsivi. Please talk to Mistress Dratha housing some healers in Tel Mora.

Humility is an uncommon trait outside of the Temple, but it is most likely not the correct tool for this task. However, I am heartened by your desire to bring charity to those in need. Please talk to Mistress Dratha about the Tel Mora healers.
A pity, I thought I sensed more dedication in you, %PCRank. Please move along.
As expected from one not of the faithful. Please move along.

I planned to compensate you for this task already, but I will adjust my plans to make sure your reward is appropriately monetary only. Are you still interested in doing this work for the Temple, %PCClass?

The last visit was from a group of Elite Ordinators headed to Ald Daedroth to deal with some cultists. No doubt Dratha felt the pressure of Almsivi that day. But even so, she has not relented and now spreads gossip. I have too many tasks to attend to here in Vivec else I would pay the old crone a visit myself. However, since you are here pursuing this rumor, perhaps you would be interested in serving the Tribunal by talking to Dratha yourself?

Where did you hear such a rumor, %PCRank? Tel Mora? Ah, well it is unsurprising that Dratha would vent her displeasure to her coven. There have been many cases of people falling ill in the area around Tel Mora. Might be the weather, the animals, some other influence? Whatever the cause, Saryoni determined it was in the best interest of our people to convince Dratha to allow some healers in her town. Against all reason, she has resisted all attempts to discuss the topic cordially.

Where did you hear such a rumor, citizen? Tel Mora? Ah, well that is unsurprising. There have been many cases of citizens falling ill in the area around Tel Mora. Might be the weather, the animals, some other influence? Whatever the cause, the Temple determined it was in the best interest of our people to convince Mistress Dratha to allow some healers in her town. Against all reason, she has resisted all attempts to discuss the topic cordially.

If anything, I would expect you to know the source of rumors like that, %PCRank. Perhaps you should speak to Berel Sala, the head of the Ordinators. This sounds like something the Ordinators would have a hand in.
I haven't heard anything about that, but you could talk to Berel Sala in the Justice Offices -- applying pressure is something the Ordinators are very proficient at.

Even if that were true, it is most likely none of your business, %PCRace. If you intend to pursue the topic anyway, I would suggest speaking with Beral Sala, the head of the Ordinators, directly. He's in the Hall of Justice. Tread lightly unless you want a quick tug up to the Ministry of Truth.
I haven't heard anything about that, %PCRank, but I would suggest you talk to someone higher up in Vivec if you really need to know more.
I haven't heard anything about that, but I would suggest you talk to someone higher up in Vivec if you really need to know more.
I had to wait what felt like ages before you came along to cure me, %PCName. This town could really use some healers.
You can find the healers in their pod behind the North side of the tower.
I heard that you're to thank for the healers being allowed to come to Tel Mora. Thank you.
Mistress Dratha is growing a new pod for the Temple healers. Isn't it exciting!
After what happened to Lette? Yes, that would be comforting.
I never planned to act as the spymaster forever. What's a promising Telvanni without some ambition? Eh, %PCRank?
I've got a few affairs to settle before I move. Should just be a few days.
That can be difficult in close quarters with a mage. You must have the agility of a fish, %PCName.
You must have formidable defenses indeed.
The mentality of an assassin. I almost feel sorry for your enemies.
The best defense is a good offense. So they say.
Yes, of course. %PCName, I'd like you to have this hood of mine. I don't imagine I will have much use for it anymore. I'll be moving to Tel Mora shortly. Perhaps I will see you there.
Uh huh. Well, anyway, I'd like you to have this old hood of mine. I don't imagine I will have much use for it anymore. I'll be moving to Tel Mora shortly. Perhaps I will see you there.

So Aryon wasn't going to tell me about the price of my swift advancement. Thank you, %PCName. I am at a disadvantage in this game. I don't know the restrictions -- or benefits -- of this geas and I have to believe that Aryon does. I will need to devote some of my time to this deadly mystery. Thank you again. I was going to give you this anyway, but know that this truly comes with my heartfelt gratitude. I want you to have my hood. I doubt I'll have much time for slinking about anymore.
You'll have to excuse my curiosity, but magical duels are one of my personal interests. What sort of preparations do you think helped the most?
Amusing, but I have to believe even a talented %PCClass like yourself encountered something memorable about the fight?
I have you to thank for it. I must know though, how was Dratha as an opponent?
Of course you have my vote, %PCName. Make House Telvanni proud!

Good grief. We've heard talk about a reborn Nerevar for years, and thought it was just Ashlander superstition. You'll have to speak directly to Master Endar about this. She lives at Tel Mora, a tower north along the coast. You should be able to find a ship at the docks to take you there for a pittance.

Yes, I understand. You are willing to take the responsibility, and I am willing to vote for you as Hortator. I think the other Telvanni councilors will also cooperate, though some might need a little persuading. Master Neloth is ill-tempered, Master Endar is a formality, and Mistress Therana is losing her mind. Archmagister Gothren is another problem. He will not refuse you directly, but will delay indefinitely. I recommend that you to kill Archmagister Gothren.
The choice of a mercenary mage. But I respect your pragmatism.
The choice of a true mage; too proud to touch coin when magical power is within reach. But I will say the scrolls I offer are worth far more than their weight in gold.

A job the Morag Tong would be happy to claim credit for, %PCName. Well done! That spy was but one of many thorns in our side, but we don't want to raise suspicion. Thank you for your help. Tell me, what does this Telvanni %PCRank desire more? Gold or enchanted scrolls?
I will hear about the fate of Chanil-Lee before you return, I assure you. Wear a helmet, give her the note, follow orders.

The enchantment is tuned to her magical signature, so any investigation by the guild should find that she miscast the summon herself and lost control. Oh, and you'll need to wear a helm. She likely has a description of you.

I knew you weren't a coward. Now, listen closely: intel from my spy in Vivec is that Chanil-Lee is expecting orders from someone in their Vivec guildhall. I want you to take her this forged note. She should leave to meet her contact in the cellar. Once she's down there, the note -- which has a special enchantment on it -- will summon a daedra which should dispatch her quickly.
Of course you do.

She's an Argonian by the name of Chanil-Lee staying at the Six Fishes in Ebonheart. I know Master Aryon wouldn't want you getting your nose too dirty with the empire right now. But if you'd like to help, I have a plan which should keep the bounty off your head.

As much as I'd like to slit their throats myself, a certain level of disengagement allows me to maintain spymaster status in secrecy. But one spy in particular has been getting too close to affairs in Vivec. Snooping around some... arrangements I made with the Temple to smooth the way for the monopoly vote.
Thanks for the sentiment...
I would, but there are none nearby.
You don't know how much this means to me. Thank you.
Thanks for the offer, but that's not a potion to cure common disease.
Thanks for the advice.
I had a run in with a mudcrab recently. Didn't realize I had caught swamp fever until I was miserable.
Thank you again for your help. For now, I will continue giving Borwen a salve to help with her headaches.

But he's a Master of Restoration! I thought for certain he would have a solution. I will have to give it some thought myself. Thank you for your help investigating this matter, %PCName. We haven't received our next stipend from the Temple yet, but Edrelle and I can offer you free healing from now on.
I'm sorry I couldn't help more.

Who knows what Dratha was trying to accomplish by focusing her memories into those stones, but we now have a root cause for what is affecting the subject. Unfortunately, even for a master such as myself, there is not much to be done now without potentially severe side effects. The subject's mind has been thoroughly damaged by the invasion of Dratha's memories. My only recommendation is for Mehra Othan to continue administering her salve to the Wood Elf.

In and of themselves, there's nothing alarming about memory stones. They are simply vessels for the captured memories of the target. But the contents of those stones are interesting. I don't think anyone has ever known Dratha's background until now. If she has history as a Mabrigash, then that means she has experience in dreams and memories. And a wizard of her power could easily -- whether intentionally or not -- broadcast her mental experiments within a relatively large area.
You think you found what's behind the mental attack on the Wood Elf in Tel Mora?
Please speak with Yakin Bael when you can. I need his input on the memory stones you found under Tel Mora.
If you find some time, I would appreciate your help.
Alright. Let me know as soon as you do.

Really? That is fascinating, %PCName. If Mistress Dratha has been using memory stones, then I wonder whether her experiments may have expanded beyond her laboratory to affect people living in Tel Mora -- namely poor Borwen. You mentioned she was training to become a Wise Woman and then turned to the way of the Mabrigash? Both groups of women are well learned in the way of dreams and memory. Would you mind bringing your findings to Kena Yakin Bael to get his advice?
Have you found anything to shed some light on Borwen's condition?
I... wish you had not told me that, %PCName. I don't know what to do with this information or how you know it, and it does not seem particularly relevant to Borwen thinking she is an Ashlander.

That's the most likely course of action to turn up a lead. I've heard there's no natural entrance to the area underneath the tower, but perhaps she keeps some type of magical key to get down there nearby. I would suggest looking for some type of artifact related to the mind or memories once you manage to get underneath the tower, but please be careful if you do venture down there. Who knows what you might find. And if Mistress Dratha catches you...

I am unclear on how to proceed, unfortunately... I doubt that Endryn Llethan would appreciate me implicating Mistress Dratha in malicious activity especially so soon after arriving here. And to be honest, I am not interested in bringing Dratha down. I simply want to help people, like Lady Almalexia does.

Well, I'm happy to hear that I correctly assessed her condition. But I am unclear on how to proceed, unfortunately... I doubt that Endryn Llethan would appreciate me implicating Mistress Dratha in malicious activity especially so soon after arriving here. And to be honest, I am not interested in bringing Dratha down. I simply want to help people like Lady Almalexia.
Yakin Bael wrote back? Wonderful! Here's something for your trouble. Let me see his letter.
You spoke with Yakin Bael? But you don't have a letter from him.
I gave you the letter for Mehra Othan already. Or do you suffer from some other ailment?
Here, take this back to the young healer.
Yes, a more thorough interview of the subject is due... here, let me write a response to Mehra Othan. Give me a moment.
You don't seem to have a letter from Mehra Othan. Whoever that is.
Let me see the letter.
Please bring my letter to Yakin Bael.
Thank you, sera. Here, please take this letter I have prepared and deliver it to Yakin Bael at the Vos Chapel. Tonas Telvani at the docks can take you to the Varo Tradehouse near Vos.

Very well. I believe that Borwen's condition is an affliction of the mind and beyond my skills as a healer. There is a Master of Restoration in the Vos Chapel just a short boat ride West from here. His name is Yakin Bael. We're too busy for me to make the trip yet, but I think this is too urgent to wait until our duties relax. Would you be willing to take a message to him?
Oh, are you interested in helping with Borwen's case now?
Please stop wasting my time.
I can understand your reluctance, %PCName. Have a good day.
Not mad in the manic sense of the term, but something is affecting her mental capacities. You see, she thinks she's an Ashlander...

You really separate the oil from the water, %PCName... yes, actually. I believe that Borwen's condition is an affliction of the mind and beyond my skills as a healer. There is a Master of Restoration in the Vos Chapel just a short boat ride west from here. His name is Yakin Bael. We're too busy for me to make the trip yet, but I think this is too urgent to wait until our duties relax. Would you be willing to take a message to him?
Your immediate hesitance to associate with this subject alarms me, %PCName. But I'll respect your wishes and won't discuss it further.

Most visits were fairly ordinary, but there was a Bosmer named Borwen who was an interesting case. She was complaining of a headache. I made her a salve of scrib jelly and dried scathecraw to rub on her temples, but I think something deep-rooted was upsetting her mental balance.
Nothing you need to be concerned about.
You first!
But... I... you... you weren't meant to see any of that! I will KILL YOU!
I... you! None of this started happening before your meddling!
Bah! A small inconvenience. It's hardly the first time a Mage Lord's experiments have caused some damage.
You have no right to judge me, child. Tel Mora is mine.
You what!?
If Dratha is capable of using geasa, then she must have been a Mabrigash.

The lord of Tel Vos wishes to remove a geas? Such a thing cannot be done. Settled people do not understand what it means to be under the thumb of fate. Except for you, Nerevarine. You bear the burden of prophecy. I will tell you about geasa.

The lord of Tel Vos wishes to remove a geas? Such a thing cannot be done. Settled people do not understand what it means to be under the thumb of fate. Though perhaps you do... I will tell you about geasa.

Thank you, %PCName. If this had been someone less dangerous, I'd have let a common assassin do the job. But I needed someone I could count on. Oh, the geas? Well, I believe that your counter reflected it back at Dratha, but with her gone, it will likely seek out the ruler of Tel Mora. A position which is currently vacant. I have naturally avoided any semblance of governing Tel Mora -- even from a distance -- for that very reason. With that said, let's talk about Endar Drenim.
You know what must be done.

I share your reservations, %PCName. But we must look to the future. Remember that the geas is but one of Dratha's tricks. She is an ancient sorceress. She will not go down without a fight. And her loyal retainers may defend her if you do not manage the situation properly.

Do not let your guard down, %PCName. The geas is but one of Dratha's tricks. She is an ancient sorceress. She will not go down without a fight. And her loyal retainers may defend her if you do not manage the situation properly.
I have known Dratha for a long time. I do not believe you can succeed. If reason fails, I hope that you will make the right decision.
Selfishness is a prominent Telvanni trait, %PCName. You wear it proudly, I see.
The Wise Woman put a counter-curse on you? I cannot easily detect wild Ashlander magic, so I will have to take your word for it. Are you ready?
Thank you, %PCName. I know you do not accept this task lightly. Seek out Sonummu Zabamat of the Zainab tribe.

%PCName, please be reasonable. She left her people to die of illness by refusing to allow healers into Tel Mora. She curses unwary visitors. She unleashed a mob of diseased vampires! What do you think could be worse than that?
That is disappointing. I will have to find a different solution in my own time.
Thank you, %PCName. Seek out Sonummu Zabamat of the Zainab tribe.

You still have other obligations and can't be hamstrung by an ancient curse, %PCName. I understand. Would you consider at least speaking to the Zainab Wise Woman? I believe she will be able to provide the means to safeguard yourself.
I understand, %PCName. The immediate danger has been dealt with. But I'm thinking about the future of Tel Mora -- don't delay too long.

The Ashlanders call a Mabrigash's curse a "geas". Dratha has woven an immensely complex geas around herself which will be released in the event of her passing. The only contemporary magic users trained to defend against geasa are Wise Women. Whoever kills Dratha will need some sort of protection. This is a serious and dangerous undertaking, %PCName. Do you accept?
Have you changed your mind, %PCRank?

It is clear that Dratha must be removed. She ignores the safety of her subjects despite being given every opportunity to intervene. If we weren't Telvanni, I might suggest a quiet retirement somewhere back on the mainland. But she will never go quietly. You've likely encountered some of Dratha's nasty curses already. Many of them are incredibly dangerous because they take root in old Mabrigash traditions which are not widely known by formal magicians and are therefore complicated to dispel in time.
It's already dead? Excellent. You are quite the warrior.

Tel Vos, Master Aryon's wizard tower, is to the west. You can't miss it. It's very strange. Tel Mora, Master Endar's wizard tower, lies across the bay on an island to the east. In Vos village, up on the hill, the Vos chapel is in the center of the village, through the gate and courtyard. Hetwoman Maela Kaushad's house is the middle house in the village, on the south. Varo Tradehouse is that big tower you see at the end of the dock.

Tel Vos, Master Aryon's wizard tower, is to the west. You can't miss it. It's very strange. Tel Mora, Master Endar's wizard tower, lies across the bay on an island to the east. In Vos village, the Vos chapel is in the center of the village, through the gate and courtyard. Hetwoman Maela Kaushad's house is the middle house on the south. Varo Tradehouse is down by the docks. Ships go to Sadrith Mora, Tel Aruhn, and Tel Mora.

He's tried to minimize the horrific implications of this spell, but I assure you that this is dangerous magic, %PCName. I believe that the reason he's not had success with it so far is that he's not giving it a specific mark. All of his energy is being dissipated into the surrounding environment instead of bending the environmental energies towards the target. If it was anyone else, I'd jot down more specific instructions, but Endar will know what to do with that much information.
Endar sent you, did he? It must be urgent if he allowed you to take his notes into this den of thieves. But nevermind that. Let me see what you brought.
The Temple has been pressuring Mistress Dratha to allow them to put some healers here in Tel Mora. Women, of course.

Well... this is better than nothing, I suppose. Thank you for your help, %PCName. This is all rather embarrassing -- duped by a Telvanni insurgent. Here, take this back as payment for your trouble. I know it isn't much, so I can promise you better prices at my shop from now on as well.
I appreciate your honesty, %PCName, but where is the rest of the money? You seem to have spent it already...

That little hobgoblin! He'll get what's coming if I have my way. Thank you for your trouble, %PCName. Unfortunately, I can't spare anything as payment. I was expecting at least some small recompense from Godros. But I'm nearly broke with this news. I'll have to increase my prices.
Did Godros have anything to say about my armor shipments?

More than one shipment? I've only just seen the two crates in the other room. I'm not sure I know what Radras means. But... hmm... Trerayna Dalen. It must have been her. Mollimo of Cloudrest mentioned that her minions were decked out in bonemold and steel armor. Please take this payment to Radras to at least cover the two crates I did receive. But I can't do anything about the ones Trerayna Dalen intercepted.

Well, now that we've solved that mystery. Please take this payment to Radras to at least cover the two crates I did receive. I can't do anything about the ones Trerayna Dalen intercepted. You should tell her not to accept any more orders which do not bear Mistress Therana's seal.

Of course! I was wondering how that upstart managed to acquire so much quality hardware for her minions. She must have been placing those orders under Godros' name and intercepting the shipments for herself at the dock! That's just fuel for the pyre she built for herself. I'll make sure the dock is secured. I'm sure Godros can work out some sort of arrangement for the smith if you speak with him.
Like I said, talk to Mollimo of Cloudrest.

More than one shipment? I've only just seen the two crates in the other room. I'm not sure I know what Radras means. But... hmm... Trerayna Dalen. It must be. Talk to Mollimo of Cloudrest. He's usually patrolling around the tower. He's been after Trerayna for weeks. This'll set him right off.
It'll stay that way until you've talked to Godros about the previous shipments.
I appreciate it, %PCName. Godros is stationed in the Tel Branora Guardpost. Please ask him about those shipments.
Well, feel free to peruse what I do have in stock.

Yes, you see, I have been fulfilling orders of steel and bonemold armor from Godros in Tel Branora under the authority of Mistress Therana, but have received nothing in return for compensation! I've lost nearly half a year's worth of income from this farce. I was resigned to my loss, but since you're here and asking about it, I'm hoping you could follow up on a note I sent with the last shipment to Godros and get to the bottom of this.

As you know from your involvement with the mages guild monopoly, things aren't as simple as casting a vote. Thank you for your help in that matter, by the way. Strategic bribes, assassinations, and spy networks are all part of politics here. Of course, in my public station, I cannot be involved with any of that directly. If you want to learn more, I suggest you speak with my stepbrother, Endar Drenim. He's been interested in talking with you.

Master Aryon mentioned that he was planning to send you my way for some instruction on politics here on Vvardenfell. So let's talk about the Grand Council. As one of five interest groups here, House Telvanni gets a single vote on the Grand Council. The others are Hlaalu, Redoran, the Temple, and the Imperial Colonists. The Telvanni Councilors each vote on internal issues at the council house in Sadrith Mora. The resolutions made there direct my actions within the Grand Council itself.

House Telvanni is represented by Galas Drenim on the Grand Council. If you're going to continue advancing in the House, I'd suggest you make her acquaintance. It's important to understand how politics work here on Vvardenfell.
House Telvanni is represented by Galas Drenim on the Grand Council. I'd like to introduce you to her after you deal with the Mages Guild monopoly.
Just return here as soon as you have them, please.

Thank you, and thank you again! And here is your payment. Truth be told, I was a bit nervous venturing out of the mushroom yet. I worry about how Dratha feels about us being here. I'm sure I'll get accustomed to our new home soon and I look forward to helping the people of Tel Mora.
I'm afraid you're missing some things.
Have you gotten the supplies from my list?
Thank you, %PCName. Here is my list. Common things. Jolda here in town might have a few of them.

I have a list of things I need, but I haven't had time to acquire them while we're still setting up here. If you could pick them up, I can refund you for your trouble with our stipend from the Temple.
You can find her at the Grand Council Chambers in Ebonheart. Take a boat to Sadrith Mora and then to Ebonheart from there.
Endar Drenim is my patron, for now. We're discussing an appropriate compensation for my part in his advancement.

Endar manages the Telvanni spy network here on Vvardenfell -- of course that isn't public knowledge and I trust you'll keep it to yourself. He's a dangerous man to make enemies with; as several assassins have learned who died by his blade or spell. He's currently living in Tel Naga, Sadrith Mora.
Out with the old and in with the new, %PCName. That's how we ensure House Telvanni is prepared for the future.

Endar isn't one to waste time, I imagine he'll be moved into Tel Mora before long. Why don't you go speak with him? I'm sure he'll be grateful. Don't neglect your allies, %PCName. Hopefully I've taught you that much.
Concerned about your reputation with Dratha's death on your hands? Really, %PCName... if anything, this only bolsters your stature. No one will stand in your way.

By now, Raven Omayn will have already announced the new Mage Lord of Tel Mora. She's been part of this plan nearly since the beginning. She's ambitious, even for a Telvanni. I'm sure she and Endar will work out some sort of advancement for her soon enough. Maybe we'll have a new spymaster.

I'm sure my plan has been clear for you. I needed a less volatile neighbor than Dratha. With her out of the picture, the path to Master of Tel Mora is clear for Endar. It won't take long for another councilor to maneuver an underling into this power vacuum, but we have the initiative. I already sent for Endar.
Endar Drenim is head spymaster for House Telvanni on Vvardenfell. What? You didn't think mages used spies? He currently lives in Tel Naga, Sadrith Mora.
Master Endar is in his throne room.
Master Endar is in the tower.
I can see Lette from here. We're staying up on the cliffs.
They got Lette! Saint's preserve me.
Welcome back to Tel Mora, %PCName. I know that things aren't very different yet. You have to take these things slowly, you know.
You'll always be welcome in Tel Mora, %PCName.
Despite what the villagers and retainers might say, the stigma against men in the city lingers like a foul odor even with Dratha being gone. It will take some effort to make changes here.
Aryon isn't a bad neighbor. But perhaps some alterations to my tower are in order to rival Tel Vos.
The roots of Tel Mora run deep. I have much still to discover of the place I now rule.
I'll see you in Tel Mora, %PCName.

%PCName, I'm glad to have you as an ally and not a rival. To be honest, I suspected Aryon's plans but I didn't know for certain much longer than you. I'm generally two steps ahead of everyone, but he's a hard man to predict. It's hard to believe that I'm the Master of Tel Mora now.
I hope those monsters can't climb up into the gardens.
Get indoors!
Those undead bastards can't climb. Hah!
They don't seem to be following us out here onto the boat.
You want to get out of here? You and me both.
Clearly you did not dispatch all of the vampires like you claimed. Get out of my sight.
As if the no men policy wasn't bad enough for local trade. Now we have vampires roaming the streets!
We're all going to die!
Why isn't Mistress Dratha doing something?
I saw a guard kill one of the monsters and it got right back up!
Those monsters came pouring out of the tower. What will we do!?
The garden is looking better every day.
Looking for quality armor, %PCRace? You'll have to excuse my limited stock.
Welcome to our humble practice. Do you need healing?
Welcome to our humble practice. We've not been here long and already the women of Tel Mora have begun stopping by for help with various ailments.
Are you in need of healing?
Are you in need of healing? Unfortunately, our supplies are still fairly thin since we've only just arrived.
You dare come here after raiding my collections? It wasn't worth my time to pursue you, but now that you're here...
Thank you so much for your help with curing Lette. The garden is recovering now too and I can start thinking about introducing more varieties of plants.

My partner, Lette, is sick and miserable for it. I haven't been able to keep up with the whole garden myself. If you have any skills in healing, we would both appreciate it if you could help her. She's down by the water on the East side of town.

Fortune favors me, %PCName. I'm %Name. Master Endar, mage-lord and Telvanni councilor, is our patron. Can I help you find your way around Tel Mora? Were you looking for specific place? Or are you looking for someone in particular?
Welcome to Tel Mora. Master Endar, mage-lord and Telvanni councilor, is our patron. Can I help you find someone in particular?

Tel Mora is the Telvanni tower of Master Endar, a newly instated wizard of the Telvanni Council. The small settlement includes a few craftsfolk and a tradehouse. Tel Mora is a good distance north along the coast. You could travel cross country, but travel by ship to Tel Mora is cheap and reliable from the Tel Aruhn docks south of here.

Tel Mora is now the wizard's tower of Master Endar, the new Telvanni mage-lord and councilor. Under his rule, men are technically allowed in the settlement again. But old habits die hard. No one here wished for Mistress Dratha to die, but things were growing increasingly uncertain and everyone feels much safer under Master Endar.
Tel Mora is the Telvanni tower of Master Endar, a new wizard of the Telvanni Council. The small settlement includes a few craftsfolk and a tradehouse.
I'm a gardener here in Tel Mora. I tend to Master Endar's alchemical gardens.
I'm a gardener here in Tel Mora. I tend to Mistress Dratha's alchemical gardens.

Services like trainers and tradesmen are in the northwest tower. We call it the Services Tower. Who wouldn't? Milar Maryon is our healer. Alenus Vendu is an enchanter. An Altmer, Andil, is our apothecary, and Mirvon Andrethi is a monk. If you need traders, smiths, or other services, the village of Vos is close by to the east, and Tel Mora, the tower of Master Endar, has a larger settlement with many merchants and tradesmen.
Stand still.
Thank you for your donation.
I'm afraid that you do not have enough coins to cover my services.
Your wounds are serious, %PCName. I can offer you healing.
Your wounds are serious, %PCName. For a small donation of 25 septims to the Temple, I can offer you healing.
I can offer you healing for your minor wounds.
For a small donation of 25 septims to the Temple, I can offer you healing for your minor wounds.
Some minor scratches, but I believe you'll be fine, %PCName.
There's not a mark on you. If you're diseased, you can ask for healing at the Shrine of Almalexia.
Master Endar is still getting settled in Tel Mora and has no chores for you.
I have no chores for you.
She isn't relevant anymore. Can't say I'll miss her.
Mistress Dratha is my patron. She lives in Tel Mora.
We are monitoring her condition.
Lette is an unfortunate example of how a Telvanni wizard's indifference can hurt those around them. Tel Mora needs healers to care for the health of Mistress Dratha's people.
She should be in the gardens.
The geas of a Mabrigash is not to be trifled with. Even killing a Mabrigash is not always enough if it is set off by her death. Best to avoid them entirely.

...I have placed the protection on you. A geas cannot be removed, but it can be countered. It's like reflecting a spell. When Dratha's geas tries to settle on you, it will be thrown back at her. Of course if she is dead... well, it's uncertain what will happen. But you should be safe.
My ancestors refused to tell me about this geas, %PCName. All geasa are forbidden, but this one must be truly harrowing. However, they did instruct me on how to perform a counter for it...
It will take time for me to prepare, %PCName.

A geas is not simply a "curse". It is a prohibition placed upon someone. If the geas is violated, the victim will suffer the consequences. But if they observe their geas, they will enjoy the blessings. Mabrigash will frequently place a geas on their male victims to control them -- and reward good behavior. Your description of this geas brings back an old memory... I must commune with my ancestors if you wish to learn more. Come back in a day.
